prompt: A survey of $200$ customers gives a $95\%$ confidence interval for a proportion with margin of error $0.06$. The manager wants a margin of error of $0.03$ at the same confidence level, and expects $\hat{p}$ to stay about the same. About how many customers should the new survey include?
hint: Think about how the margin of error depends on $n$. It shrinks with the square root of the sample size, not with $n$ itself.

hints.text: Think about how the margin of error depends on $n$. It shrinks with the square root of the sample size, not with $n$ itself.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: going from $n = 100$ to $n = 400$ doubles $\sqrt{n}$ from 10 to 20, so the margin of error halves. Multiply $n$ by 4 to halve the margin.
Going from $0.06$ to $0.03$ halves the margin, which needs $\sqrt{n}$ to double. So $n$ must be multiplied by $2^2 = 4$: work out $4 \times 200$.
$4 \times 200 = 800$, so the new survey should include about $800$ customers.

explanation: The margin of error is $z^* \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}$. With $z^*$ and $\hat{p}$ fixed, it is proportional to $1/\sqrt{n}$.
Cutting the margin from $0.06$ to $0.03$ halves it, so $\sqrt{n}$ must double, and that means $n$ must quadruple.
The new sample size is $4 \times 200 = 800$ customers. Doubling to 400 would only shrink the margin to about $0.042$.
